headline: Why did I give my best years to someone who wasn't my soulmate?
note:
FRAME: soulmate x age band. NO MAN EXISTS YET — she asks WHEN or WHETHER. Must not fall through to decode-him.
🔴 THE AGE BAND LIVES IN THE AD SET, NEVER IN THE COPY. No age, no number, no life-stage.
🔴 NO DURATION, forward or back — 'not much longer' is a LENGTH, and a length is not a date.
⚠ SHE is the subject of beats 3-6; the male figure is described in beats 1-2 and retired there.
⚠ NO FAMILY-LINE LANGUAGE anywhere in the read.

🔴 THE HARDEST BEAT 4 IN THE FAMILY. Her ad states the years went to the wrong person, so the read may say it — but it must not grade the man, grade her choice, or hand her a consolation that reads as ranking two loves. It acquits the years instead: nothing she gave was wasted.
⛔ No verdict on the ex, in either direction.

readback.1 would a person say this: Yes. 'And those years are behind you' is honest without being bleak.
readback.2 is every noun real: Nothing going spare on the table, the still-growing wood, the mid-step feet — all on the card.
readback.3 anything she could catch me getting wr: No. Beat 4 says it was not him and those years are behind her. Her ad says both outright.
readback.4 does the symbol prove the line at a gl: Yes. Wood that kept growing the whole time it hung proves 'you weren't standing still'.
readback.5 does the card mean what TAROT_CARD_VOC: Yes — the Hanged Man is read as suspension WITH life in it, which is exactly Waite's point.

a: You turned the Magician. You couldn't see them, and your hand went to the worker of the three.
Look at his hands. Both are busy, and neither one is resting.
You asked why your best years went to someone who wasn't your soulmate. The thing I keep looking at is how much work is here.
What troubles me is that they went to someone who wasn't the one. And you're the one left with the question.
Something sits in the way of this, close in rather than far off. I don't think it started with you.
Let me look closer at what's sitting there…
b: You turned the Hanged Man. Nothing showed which was which, and you took the one held by one rope.
Look at the rope. One ankle holds him, and nothing else does.
You asked why your best years went to someone who wasn't your soulmate. The rope runs up into the beam, and that's what I'm reading.
And yet they went to someone who wasn't the one. You're the one asking what those years were for.
Something arrives at the point where things would settle. I don't think any of it began with you.
Let me look closer at what that is…
c: You turned the Fool. The backs gave nothing away, and you chose the one travelling light.
Look at the bundle on his stick. That's all he's taking with him.
You asked why your best years went to someone who wasn't your soulmate. A start made with very little — that's what this one shows me.
They went to someone who wasn't the one, though. And you're the one asking why.
Whatever holds this holds it steady, and it hasn't shifted. I don't think it began with you.
Let me look closer at what's holding this…
